description: Law clerks will have the opportunity to work with the Committee's policy, oversight, and investigative teams, conducting legal and policy research, reviewing documents, and preparing materials for hearings, markups, and other Committee activities. The fall clerkship period runs from September to December. Preference will be given to candidates who are available at least three days per week. This is a paid position, and the Committee is happy to work with applicants seeking academic credit.
responsibilities: Conduct legal and policy research with the Committee's policy, oversight, and investigative teams
Review documents
Prepare materials for hearings, markups, and other Committee activities
qualifications: Current law student
Strong research and writing skills
Enthusiastic about the Committee's mission to protect the homeland and strengthen national security
Available at least three days per week (preferred)
how_to_apply: Submit a resume, brief cover letter, and writing sample to CHSJobs@mail.house.gov with the subject line "Fall Law Clerkship." Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

position_title: Internship for House Committee on Veterans' Affairs - Majority Staff
description: House Committee on Veterans' Affairs has a need to hire Fall interns in the Washington, D.C. office in a full-time capacity. Interested candidates are encouraged to submit a resume and cover letter. Once the application period closes, the office will contact the best qualified candidates to begin our interview process. Interns provide support with a variety of committee activities, including administrative and logistical support for hearings, business meetings, and mark-ups; assisting the committee's communications team with media relations activities; and conducting legislative research for policy issues within the committee's jurisdiction.
responsibilities: Provides administrative and logistical support to ensure Committee hearings, business meetings, and mark-ups are run in an efficient and effective manner
Serves as an initial point of contact for visitors (e.g., hearing witnesses, government officials, and other VIPs) who have business with the Committee and its staff
Answers phone calls and routes mail and other messages to appropriate committee staff for further action
Partners with the committee staff to prepare stakeholder inquiries on oversight and policy issue areas within the committee's jurisdiction
Edits Legislative Transcripts
Performs research on issues or topics related to public law, regulation, and legislation
Attends meetings with stakeholders and assists the legislative staff prepare for hearings and mark-ups
Assisting the committee's communications team with media relations activities
qualifications: Adaptability: Adapts quickly to change or unexpected obstacles
Research and Analysis: Collects, synthesizes, and analyzes information from a variety of stakeholders and sources in an objective, unbiased manner to inform strategic decision making
Planning and Coordination: Coordinates with others to accomplish goals; monitors progress and evaluates outcomes
Interpersonal Skills: Shows understanding, courtesy, tact, empathy, and politeness
Written Communication: Writes in a clear, concise, organized, and convincing manner for the intended audience
Pursuing or completed Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience
Prior stakeholder service or customer relationship management experience is preferred
A demonstrated interest in public service
how_to_apply: All interested candidates are encouraged to submit a cover letter and resume by 08/12/2026 to VAR.resumes@mail.house.gov
equal_opportunity: All applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including marital or parental status), sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, or national origin.

description: Representative Seth Magaziner (RI-02) seeks part-time, paid Fall 2026 interns for his Warwick, Rhode Island office, to start at the beginning of September and go until end of December. Duties include providing a welcoming environment to constituents, answering incoming calls, assisting Member and key staff with logistical and administrative duties, receiving and logging constituent input on policy matters, conducting research and drafting correspondence, assisting with planning and execution of Member's public outreach, and accompanying district staff to public forums, meetings, and events.
responsibilities: Provides a welcoming environment and positive first impression of the Member office to constituents, visitors, and other VIPs
Answers incoming calls with poise, professionalism, and promptness
Assists Member and key staff (e.g. Staff Assistant, Press Assistant, Constituent Services Team) with logistical and administrative duties
Receives and logs input from constituents on policy matters for the Member office's consideration and response
Conducts research, and drafts correspondence and memoranda
Assists with planning and execution of Member's public outreach at local events
Accompanies district staff to public forums, meetings, and events as a representative to the Member
qualifications: Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Professional phone manner and customer service orientation
Ability to conduct research and draft correspondence and memoranda
Organizational skills and attention to detail
Interest in constituent services and public outreach
Availability for part-time work from September through December

description: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Democratic Staff seeks a motivated and reliable Video Production Intern this fall. Interns will be responsible for helping with clipping streams of sessions, editing and captioning videos, helping with shoots, scripting content and other administrative tasks as assigned. Successful candidates will possess extreme familiarity with Adobe Premiere Pro. Additional experiences with Adobe After Effects and Photoshop are a plus. Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapid response environment is a must. Candidates will be expected to work in-person in Washington, DC, with opportunities for remote work during Congressional recesses. Full-time candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences are strongly encouraged to apply.
responsibilities: Clipping streams of sessions
Editing and captioning videos
Helping with shoots
Scripting content
Other administrative tasks as assigned
qualifications: Extreme familiarity with Adobe Premiere Pro
Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapid response environment
Additional experience with Adobe After Effects and Photoshop is a plus
how_to_apply: Send a resume, portfolio, and your availability this fall to ethan.cesar@mail.house.gov and OversightPress@mail.house.gov.

description: Congresswoman Doris Matsui, representing the 7th Congressional District of California, seeks interns for her Washington, D.C. office for the Fall 2026 term. The Press and Digital Intern will help communicate the Congresswoman's work through social media, graphics, photography, video, and other digital content. This position is well suited for a creative candidate who is interested in public service and eager to build communications experience in a congressional office. Press Intern responsibilities will vary but may include answering phones and data entry. Washington DC interns may be asked to assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff, attending briefings, hearings, and markups, and responding to constituent correspondence. Ties to California's 7th District are preferred, but not required. All applications are considered on a rolling basis.
responsibilities: Help communicate the Congresswoman's work through social media, graphics, photography, video, and other digital content
Answer phones and perform data entry
Assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff
Attend briefings, hearings, and markups
Respond to constituent correspondence
qualifications: Strong writing, editing, and social media instincts
Familiarity with Canva, photography, video editing, or graphic design
An interest in digital marketing, audience engagement, or social media analytics
Strong media literacy, attention to detail, and sound judgment
An ability to listen closely, follow instructions, learn through observation and a willingness to try new approaches
Basic familiarity with graphic design/video editing software
Experience in a press or digital media role (including internships) preferred but not required
Ties to California's 7th District preferred, but not required
how_to_apply: Visit the Internships page of Congresswoman Matsui's official website and complete the application form at https://matsui.house.gov/services/internships. A cover letter, resume, and 2 writing samples (1 writing sample & 1 graphic example preferred, but not required) must be submitted as part of the application.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.

description: A senior Republican Representative serving on the House Financial Services Committee is seeking interns for the Fall of 2026 in their Washington D.C. office. Interns will gain a strong understanding of the functions of a congressional office and firsthand experience with the legislative process. Internship start and end dates are flexible and part-time internships are available for students. Full-time hours are Monday-Friday 9:00-5:00. This is a paid opportunity with a monthly stipend and reimbursement for Metro commute. Intern responsibilities include, but are not limited to, answering phones, assisting with constituent correspondence, conducting legislative research, leading Capitol tours, attending hearings and briefings and drafting memos. Applicants should be detail oriented, able to work well in a fast-paced environment, have strong oral and written communication skills and an interest in public policy. Pennsylvania ties are preferred but not required. To apply, please send a resume and cover letter to: Kieran.Patch@mail.house.gov.
